properties.description:
THE LESSON, and it is about instruments measuring themselves. This design's coverage line read "241/288 capability(ies) verified" for months. Measured on 2026-09-22: 21 of those 241 had a check anything could re-run. The code was at 85% line coverage the same day. So the record was wrong in BOTH directions at once — it understated the testing that existed and overstated the testing it could prove — and neither error was visible from inside, because `has_executable_form` was already computed, already reported per check in the loop digest, and never rolled up to the number anybody read.

WHAT LANDED: the count split (`capabilities_verified_by_runnable_check`, said as its own sentence and said when zero), and the ratchet (`tools/check_verification_ratchet.py`) that grandfathers the 220 by id and forbids a 221st.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO: backfill. Writing 220 tests to make a number green is the behaviour the number exists to detect.

AND ONE THING FOUND SIDEWAYS: `link_artifact` draws REALIZES and only REALIZES, so the discoverable way to "register the file that is the check" produces no executable form at all. The IMPLEMENTS edge is a separate call nothing asks for. That is a plausible cause of the 282, and it was met by hand while writing the test that pins the split.
properties.name: "Verified" splits into a check something re-runs and a check somebody typed, and the claim-only set ratchets
